page: Microsoft Azure E128-32ads_v7 is a memory-optimized server belonging to the Eadsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a high memory-to-vCPU ratio, equipped with 1024.0 GB of RAM and 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical AMD EPYC 9V45 cores. The processor operates at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, featuring 32 MB of L3 cache and supporting advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and cryptography acceleration.

The server includes 7559 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, making it highly capable for data-intensive operations. In benchmark evaluations, the single-core performance is top-tier, as demonstrated by stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also rank in the top 10%. Multi-core performance and memory bandwidth benchmarks generally fall into the average to strong ranges, with static web serving throughput showing strong performance.

While the server excels in memory capacity and single-core execution, its multi-threaded scaling and large-model LLM inference represent clear tradeoffs. For instance, LLM text generation with a large 70B model is poor, registering only 2.44 tokens per second. However, smaller model inference and general memory-bound tasks perform well. This hardware profile offers high resource density, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient choice for memory-intensive workloads without the overhead of dedicated GPU hardware. It is highly suited for large databases, in-memory caching systems, software compilation, and data-intensive enterprise applications.
description: Microsoft Azure E128-32ads_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the Eadsv7 family, powered by a 4.5 GHz AMD EPYC 9V45 processor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs (16 physical cores), 1024.0 GB of RAM, and a substantial 7559 GB local NVMe SSD. Operating on Microsoft Hyper-V, this x86_64 server delivers top-tier single-core performance, outstanding single-threaded compression speeds, and strong software compilation capabilities. However, multi-core scaling and large-model LLM inference show relative performance tradeoffs. With its massive memory-to-CPU ratio and high-capacity local storage, this server is highly cost-efficient for memory-bound enterprise workloads. It is best suited for large-scale databases, in-memory caching, and data-intensive applications.
